slides.title: Circular Dependency Leak
slides.prompt: What structural problem occurs when two objects hold std::shared_ptr to each other?
options: Circular reference preventing reference count from reaching zero (Memory Leak)
Automatic crash due to double delete
slides.correctAnswer: Circular reference preventing reference count from reaching zero (Memory Leak)

slides.title: Unique Check Method

slides.title: make_shared Efficiency Advantage
slides.prompt: Why is std::make_shared preferred over std::shared_ptr<T>(new T())?
options: Performs single memory allocation for both control block and object
Allows raw pointers to be cast implicitly
slides.correctAnswer: Performs single memory allocation for both control block and object

slides.title: Aliasing Constructor Concept
slides.prompt: shared_ptr can store stored pointer and owned pointer separately. Fill in type parameter.

slides.title: Thread Safety of Reference Count
slides.prompt: Are reference count increments/decrements in std::shared_ptr thread-safe?
options: Yes, reference count updates are atomic
No, external mutex locks are always required
Only when compiled with multithread flag
slides.correctAnswer: Yes, reference count updates are atomic
